statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits at the top of the low band while Stress stays elevated on the long-end rate selloff.
recommendation: Conditions are mean-reverting: today's opening gap was fully retraced and volatility is decaying. Stress remains elevated because the 30-year yield is at a 2004 high, and the US power hour into the cash close is flagged as the narrow danger window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 retraces its opening gap as the bond rout continues; Tail low, Stress elevated
body: NDX opened at 30,225 against a 30,470 prior close, set the session low at 30,204 and then recovered through the prior close to a 30,529 high, trading near 30,433 at the assessment cutoff. The gap was fully retraced and VIX has eased from a 16.57 high to 15.48, so retracements are occurring and mean reversion is functioning. The macro backdrop is nonetheless hostile: the 30-year Treasury yield reached roughly 5.44%, its highest since 2004, the 10-year traded near 5.11-5.14%, its highest since July 2007, and markets have moved to price a meaningful probability of a further Fed hike in October after New York Fed President Williams described that expectation as a reasonable way of thinking about it. Today's US data reinforced the hawkish read: initial jobless claims came in at 197K against a 201K forecast and new home sales at 0.684M against 0.626M expected. WTI rose about 3% to roughly $94.9 after peaking near $97, then trimmed on signs the US and Iran may re-establish Persian Gulf exports, so the oil impulse is conflicting rather than aligned. Conflicting cross-asset signals with observed two-way NQ structure keep Tail in the low band while Stress stays elevated. Shared Finviz context was collected at 12:21Z with partial status and no futures or calendar section, so at over five hours old it was treated as stale and used for headline discovery only; all levels here come from independent current research.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours ran in a persistent watch band. Published Tail sat at 24 through the late European and US afternoon of 23 September, eased to 17-20 across the Asian overnight as conditions normalised, then rebuilt to a 25 peak at 09:00 UTC on a trend-down European session driven by the bond selloff. It has since oscillated between 20 and 24 with a mixed dominant mode, and the most recent published hour read 20. Stress held between 49 and 58 throughout, confirming a difficult but consistently mean-reverting environment rather than a pathological one-way path.
outlookSummary: The base case is continued two-way trade inside today's 30,204-30,529 range, with conditional Tail lifted into the watch band only for the 19:00-20:15 UTC power hour and cash close, where late-session repositioning against multi-decade-high yields is most plausible. Conditional Tail then eases through the post-close and Asian overnight to the mid-teens absent a fresh catalyst. It rebuilds into Friday's 12:30 UTC durable goods release and the 13:30 UTC US cash open, which together form the highest conditional-risk pairing of the forecast because opening-auction continuation after a data surprise is the pattern most capable of denying retracement. That window is a scheduled checkpoint, not observed structure. The reading would be understated if NQ were to hold near a session extreme on shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements; it would ease further if long-end yields stabilise and volatility keeps decaying.
